claims.text: Integrating machine learning with atomic-scale descriptors of chemical disorder can identify HEAs with intrinsically low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than conventional models.
The proposed accuracy improvement arises from capturing complex phonon-scattering effects caused by configurational disorder.
Arc-melted and annealed HEAs have a homogenized, randomly distributed elemental microstructure representative of typical disordered HEAs.
Local chemical environments, mixing enthalpy, and short-range-order parameters are descriptors sensitive to atomic-scale disorder.
Testing from 300 to 800 K in an inert atmosphere ensures that measured thermal transport is dominated by phonon conduction.
Local atomic-scale disorder and short-range order in a multielement lattice strongly influence phonon scattering.
Nonlinear interactions among multiple elements enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering suppresses thermal conductivity.
Disorder-sensitive descriptors represent scattering and thermal-conductivity suppression better than rule-of-mixtures or mean-field models.
The proposed approach will provide at least 20% higher prediction accuracy than conventional models.
The proposed approach will consistently identify HEAs having lower phonon thermal conductivity.
Conventional rule-of-mixtures and mean-field models do not explicitly incorporate atomic-scale disorder effects.
The approach is reliable only within HEA composition ranges having mixing enthalpy and chemical disorder within typical bounds.
Extreme elemental fractions, phase separation, or ordering may reduce the approach's predictive accuracy.
Processing-induced microstructural variations may affect the magnitude of the prediction improvement.
The model should be benchmarked against conventional models using compositionally varied, consistently processed HEAs measured by laser flash analysis from 300 to 800 K.
Failure to reduce prediction error by at least 20% relative to conventional models falsifies the hypothesis.
The hypothesis is also falsified if more than 70% of samples have measured-to-predicted conductivity deviations greater than 30%.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as having a random elemental distribution, while short-range order is treated as an associated structural feature and predictive descriptor. A perfectly random distribution has no nonrandom short-range order, so the intended initial degree of ordering is unclear.

The prediction is framed as at least 20% higher accuracy, whereas falsification is defined using at least a 20% reduction in prediction error. These are not necessarily equivalent without a specified accuracy or error metric.
